web.form.replications.text: Blocks, or plots of each treatment

report.design.layoutSupplied.text: supplied with the trial, not randomised here

report.checks.arrangement.imbricated.text: Untreated strips between the plots; they show the pest pressure and are left out of the analysis above.

report.checks.arrangement.adjacent.text: Each plot is halved and one half left untreated; the analysis above uses the treated halves.

report.checks.arrangement.paired.text: Each treated plot has its own untreated partner; the analysis above uses the treated plots.

report.splitPlot.separation.text: Mean separation: {method} (alpha = {alpha}), on this factor's own error. Effect {significance} (P {probability}).

report.twoFactor.lettersNote.text: Letters in a row compare the {second} levels at that {first} level.

report.twoFactor.noLettersNote.text: No letters: the {first} × {second} interaction is not significant, so the levels are compared through each factor's means above.

report.twoFactor.secondWithinFirst.text: LSD (alpha = {alpha}) between two {second} levels at the same {first} level

report.twoFactor.firstWithinSecond.text: LSD (alpha = {alpha}) between two {first} levels at the same {second} level

report.reproducibility.splitPlotMethodVa.text: Split-plot ANOVA; {test} on each factor's own error (alpha = {alpha})

report.assessment.notNumeric.text: Not analysed: AOV requires a numeric assessment (this assessment is {dataType}).

report.check.excluded.text: The untreated check ({check}) is left out of this analysis; its mean as recorded is {mean}.

report.missing.leastSquares.text: Missing plots: {plots}. They are left out, and the model is fitted by least squares to the plots that have a value (missing-plot policy leastSquares). The treatment means below are adjusted (least-squares) means.

report.missing.estimate.text: Missing plots: {plots}. For the arithmetic only, each is given Yates' estimate, the value that makes the error sum of squares smallest (missing-plot policy estimate). An estimate is not an observation and is never stored. The treatment means below are those of the completed table, which are the adjusted means.

report.missing.closedForm.text: With one missing plot the estimate is Yates' closed form.

report.missing.iterated.text: The estimates were reached by Yates' iteration in {cycles} cycles, stopping when none moved by more than {tolerance} of the spread of the values present (their largest departure from their mean); the starting values and the order are fixed, so the estimates are reproducible.

report.anova.transformedScale.text: Analysed on the {scale} scale; the table, grand mean, and CV below are on that scale.

report.anova.typeIIIBlocks.text: Sums of squares are Type III: block is adjusted for treatment and treatment for block, so the lines do not add up to the total.

report.anova.typeIIINoBlocks.text: The treatments are unequally replicated. The treatment sum of squares is Type III, which with a single factor is also the sequential one, so the lines add up to the total.

report.anova.completedTable.text: Sums of squares are those of the completed table, and the degrees of freedom for error and for total are each reduced by {count}. The treatment sum of squares is reduced by {bias}, the upward bias the estimates give it, and the total with it. The block line is not corrected and is not tested.

report.anova.adjustedGrandMean.text: Grand mean (of the adjusted treatment means)

report.anova.coefficientOfVariationAdjus.text: Coefficient of variation (on the adjusted grand mean)

report.means.backTransformNote.text: Means are back-transformed to the original scale as point estimates (not symmetric intervals); the analysis of variance and mean separation were computed on the {scale} scale.

report.means.notSeparated.text: Means were not separated: the treatment effect was not significant (protected LSD).

report.pairs.note.text: With missing plots the standard error of a difference depends on the pair, so each pair is held to a critical difference of its own.

report.pairs.tukeyKramerInBlocks.text: For adjusted means in blocks the Tukey-Kramer test holds its error rate only approximately.

report.chart.whiskers.text: Bars are means; whiskers are one standard error of a mean ({error}), from the error of the analysis.

report.chart.whiskersTransformed.text: Bars are means back-transformed to the original scale; whiskers are one standard error ({error} on the {scale} scale), back-transformed, so they need not be symmetric.

report.chart.whiskersEach.text: Bars are means; whiskers are one standard error of each mean ({low} to {high}, as their plots differ in number), from the error of the analysis.

report.chart.whiskersEachTransformed.text: Bars are means back-transformed to the original scale; whiskers are one standard error of each mean ({low} to {high} on the {scale} scale, as their plots differ in number), back-transformed, so they need not be symmetric.

report.chart.letters.text: Bars sharing a letter do not differ significantly.

report.chart.againstCheck.text: The table above compares each treatment with {check}.

report.assumptions.note.text: Reported only; these do not change the analysis above (significance level alpha = {alpha}).

report.assumptions.residualsNote.rcbd.text: Residuals are from the additive block-and-treatment model and are constrained (they sum to zero within each block and each treatment), so the normality test is approximate.

report.assumptions.residualsNote.crd.text: Residuals are each plot's value less its treatment mean; they sum to zero within each treatment, so the normality test is approximate.

report.assumptions.residualsNote.splitPl.text: Main-plot residuals come from the main-plot means after the block and main-plot effects (error a); subplot residuals are each plot's departure from its main plot after the combination effects (error b). Both are constrained, so the normality tests are approximate.

report.dunnett.separation.text: Each treatment against {check} by Dunnett's two-sided test (alpha = {alpha}). Treatment effect {significance} (P {probability}).

report.means.dunnettDifferenceByTreatmen.text: Critical difference (Dunnett, alpha = {alpha}), which differs by treatment

report.reproducibility.missingLeastSquar.text: {assessment}: least squares on the plots present, Type III sums of squares, adjusted means, each comparison on its own standard error; left out: {plots}

report.reproducibility.missingEstimate.text: {assessment}: Yates' estimates on the analysed scale (cycles {cycles}, tolerance {tolerance}), completed-table sums of squares with treatment reduced by {bias}, each comparison on its own standard error; {plots}

web.footer.offline.text: Runs offline. Your data stays on this machine.

web.trials.empty.text: No trials yet. Add one to get started.

web.add.intro.text: Paste a trial package as JSON, or choose a file. This is the trial's canonical design; the layout is randomized from its seed.

web.form.intro.text: Fill in the trial, its treatments and its assessments. Trials with product lines, applications, factors or untreated checks are written as a trial file.

web.form.layoutGenerate.text: Lay the trial out here (randomised complete blocks)

web.form.seedHelp.text: Leave empty for a new one; it is recorded with the trial.

web.form.layoutHelp.text: A CSV with the columns plotNumber, block, positionInBlock and treatmentCode, one row per plot.

web.form.assessmentsHelp.text: For numbers, give the unit and the lowest and highest values expected. For categories, list them separated by commas.

web.form.problem.number.text: Assessment row {row}: {field} is not a number.

web.form.problem.replications.text: The number of blocks is a whole number.

web.form.problem.seed.text: The seed is a whole number.

web.form.problem.layoutFile.text: Choose the layout file to upload.

web.trial.layoutIntro.text: Plots as drilled in the field, grouped by block. Randomised from seed {seed}.

web.trial.layoutIntroSupplied.text: Plots as drilled in the field, grouped by block. This layout was supplied with the trial.

web.trial.enterIntro.text: Type values plot by plot. Each one is checked as it is saved.

web.entry.intro.text: One value per plot. Leave a box empty for no value. Nothing is saved until every value is accepted.

web.entry.refusedHeading.text: Nothing was saved: the marked values cannot be accepted.

web.entry.confirmHeading.text: Nothing was saved yet: the marked values are outside the expected values. Tick each one you want to keep, then save again.

web.entry.outOfRange.text: Outside the expected values; keep it

web.entry.refused.twoDecimalMarks.text: Written with both a point and a comma.

web.import.intro.text: Upload the collected data as a CSV file or an Excel workbook (.xlsx). You see the table and say which column holds what before anything is saved.

web.place.none.text: There is no {level} to put a trial in yet. Add one first:

web.places.intro.text: Trials live in places: {levels}, then the trial. Roles and settings are given by place.

web.places.noLevels.text: This store has no hierarchy levels: trials stand on their own.

web.account.tokenIntro.text: A token lets a script act as you through the API (Authorization: Bearer <token>).

web.account.tokenNeedsName.text: Say what the token is for.

web.account.tokenShownOnce.text: Your new token, shown this once; copy it now:

web.importFile.previewIntro.text: {file}: {rows} rows; the first ten are shown. Say how the file is laid out and which column holds what. Nothing is saved until you press Import.

web.importFile.shapeLegend.text: How the file is laid out

web.importFile.shapeWide.text: One row per plot, one column per assessment

web.importFile.shapeLong.text: One row per value, with columns for the plot, the assessment and the value

web.importFile.wideIntro.text: Under each column heading, choose the assessment it holds, or leave it ignored.

web.importFile.longIntro.text: The assessment column must hold the trial's assessment codes: {codes}.

web.importFile.problem.decimal.text: Choose the decimal mark the file uses.

web.importFile.problem.plotColumn.text: Choose the column that holds the plot numbers.

web.importFile.problem.noAssessmentColum.text: Choose the assessment at least one column holds.

web.importFile.problem.repeatedAssessmen.text: Two columns are set to the same assessment; each assessment can come from one column only.

web.importFile.problem.longColumns.text: Choose the columns that hold the plot numbers, the assessment codes and the values.

web.importFile.problem.sameColumn.text: The plot, the assessment and the value must come from three different columns.

web.importFile.problem.shape.text: Choose how the file is laid out.

web.importFile.wideSubsamples.text: An assessment that takes subsamples can take several columns, one per subsample, in the order of the file: {codes}.

web.entry.subsamples.text: Each plot takes {count} subsamples; the plot's value is {rule}.

report.subsamples.mean.text: Each plot's value is the mean of its {count} subsamples, over those recorded.

report.subsamples.sum.text: Each plot's value is the sum of its {count} subsamples.

report.subsamples.short.text: Plots short of subsamples, their mean taken over the rest: {plots}.

web.weather.intro.text: Upload a CSV of days: a date column (YYYY-MM-DD), then any of rainfall, irrigation, minimumTemperature and maximumTemperature with the unit in brackets, e.g. rainfall [mm], and notes. It replaces the trial's weather log.

web.weather.result.text: The weather log now holds {count} days.

web.report.intro.text: The AOV Means Table and reproducibility record for every numeric assessment.

web.trial.noObservations.text: No observations yet. Import some to run the analysis.

web.verify.intro.text: Export the trial and re-import it; the content hash must match.

web.verify.pass.text: Reproducibility check passed. The trial exports and re-imports to the same content hash.

web.verify.fail.text: Reproducibility check failed: the re-imported hash does not match.

web.delete.confirmIntro.text: This permanently removes the trial and all its observations. It cannot be undone.

diagnostic.nonAdditivity.flagged.text: Significant non-additivity; the additive RCBD model may be inadequate

diagnostic.notComputed.needsTwoByTwo.text: not computed: needs at least two treatments and two plots of each

diagnostic.notComputed.noDeviationVariat.text: not computed: no within-treatment variation in absolute deviations

diagnostic.notComputed.tooFewErrorDegree.text: not computed: too few error degrees of freedom for the one-df test

diagnostic.notComputed.noTreatmentOrBloc.text: not computed: no treatment or no block variation

diagnostic.notComputed.noRemainderVariat.text: not computed: no residual variation after the non-additivity term

diagnostic.notComputed.tooFewResiduals.text: not computed: only {count} residuals (need at least {minimum})

diagnostic.notComputed.zeroResidualSprea.text: not computed: residuals have zero spread

diagnostic.recommendation.forKind.text: assumptions were flagged and this is {kind} data; a {transform} transform may help. Declare it on the assessment -- it is never applied automatically.

diagnostic.recommendation.generic.text: assumptions were flagged; if this is count or proportion data, declaring a measurementKind and a variance-stabilizing transform on the assessment may help (transforms are never applied automatically).

report.draftNotice.text: Draft translation (machine-generated, not yet reviewed): wording may be imprecise. Numbers, identifiers, and the content hash are unaffected.

web.locale.draftNotice.text: This translation is an unreviewed machine draft; wording may be imprecise.

web.signOut.atProviderFailed.text: You are signed out of OpenFurrow, but signing out at {provider} failed: {reason}

web.signOut.fromProviderRefused.text: The sign-out request from {provider} was refused: {reason}

web.signOut.notAnswer.text: This is not a sign-out message from {provider}.

web.tasks.intro.text: Work the scheduler does on a schedule, or at once when asked. A schedule is a five-field cron expression (minute, hour, day of the month, month, day of the week), read in the server's time zone.

web.tasks.scheduler.never.text: No scheduler has checked in, so nothing scheduled runs. Start one beside the web server with: openfurrow scheduler

web.tasks.scheduler.late.text: The scheduler last checked in {seconds} seconds ago. It may have stopped; nothing scheduled runs while it is stopped.

web.tasks.scheduler.seen.text: The scheduler checked in {seconds} seconds ago.

web.task.isEnabled.text: Enabled: it runs on its schedule.

web.task.isDisabled.text: Disabled: it does not run on its schedule, but can be run now.

web.tasks.none.text: No tasks yet. A task is made with the feature that needs it, such as a federation provider read from a discovery aggregate.

web.task.scheduleHelp.text: Read in the server's time zone, {zone}. For example: 0 */6 * * * is every six hours, 30 2 * * * is daily at 02:30, 0 7 * * mon is Mondays at 07:00.

web.task.done.disable.text: Disabled: it no longer runs on its schedule.

web.task.done.run.text: Run requested. The scheduler starts it when it next checks in.

web.task.problem.minutes.text: the time limit is a whole number of minutes

web.administration.intro.text: Who may do what, how the server is set up, and what has been done. Each section shows to the people who may use it.

web.administration.index.nothing.text: Nothing in the administration area is yours to use.

web.administration.confirmNeeded.text: Tick the box to confirm, then try again.

web.administration.about.accounts.text: The people who sign in here: add an account, set a password, deactivate one, link it to an identity provider.

web.administration.about.groups.text: Accounts gathered so that a role is given to all of them at once. A group mirrored from an identity provider is that provider's to change.

web.administration.about.roles.text: Named sets of permissions. Five are built in; define your own from the same permissions.

web.administration.about.assignments.text: Every role given: to an account, a group or a workload rule, at the server, a place or a trial. A role holds where it is given and below.

web.administration.about.settings.text: Each setting's value at the server, a place or a trial, and where that value comes from. The nearest value applies: the trial, its places from the innermost out, the server, then the default.

web.administration.about.signInMode.text: Whether everyone who reaches the server may do everything, or each person signs in and holds the roles given to them.

web.administration.about.providers.text: Where people sign in besides this site, and what provisions accounts: OpenID Connect, SAML, research federations, CAS, LDAP and SCIM.

web.administration.about.workloads.text: Rules that let a CI or cloud job call the API with its platform's own short-lived token instead of a stored one.

web.administration.about.tasks.text: Work the scheduler does on a schedule: see the runs, change a schedule, run a task now, add or delete one.

web.administration.about.audit.text: Every change, who made it, from where and what it changed, newest first.

web.administration.done.deactivated.text: Deactivated: its sessions and API tokens are ended.

web.administration.done.cleared.text: Cleared: the value now comes from further out.

web.administration.unknown.providerKind.text: “{name}” is not a kind of identity provider.

web.administration.unknown.taskKind.text: “{name}” is not a kind of task.

web.administration.unknown.scope.text: “{name}” is not the server, a place or a trial you may see.

web.administration.assignments.chooseHol.text: Choose who the role is given to: an account, a group or a workload rule.

web.administration.permission.view.text: See trials, places and their settings

web.administration.permission.manageAcce.text: Manage accounts, groups, roles, identity providers and workload rules

web.administration.accounts.userNameHelp.text: 2 to 64 letters of any script, digits, '.', '_', '@' and '-'. It is kept in lower case.

web.administration.accounts.passwordHelp.text: Leave empty for an account that signs in through an identity provider only.

web.administration.account.deactivateInt.text: A deactivated account cannot sign in, and its sessions and API tokens end at once. Its history in the audit log stays.

web.administration.account.reactivateInt.text: This account is deactivated: it cannot sign in.

web.administration.account.identitiesInt.text: The identity each provider knows this person by. A sign-in through a provider reaches this account by its link.

web.administration.account.subject.text: The provider's subject for the person

web.administration.account.subjectHelp.text: The provider's own stable identifier: the OpenID Connect sub, the SAML persistent NameID, or the directory user name.

web.administration.account.rolesIntro.text: The roles given to this account, and those it holds through its groups, which are changed on the group's page.

web.administration.group.mirrored.text: This group is mirrored from the identity provider {provider}, which alone sets its members and removes it. Roles are given to it here like to any group.

web.administration.roles.codeHelp.text: A lower-case letter, then letters and digits, such as fieldLead. It cannot be changed afterwards.

web.administration.roles.exists.text: A role “{code}” exists already; change it on its own page.

web.administration.role.deleteIntro.text: A role still given to someone is not deleted; take it back from everyone first.

web.administration.settings.readOnly.text: You may read the settings here; changing them needs the permission to change settings at this place.

web.administration.settings.notAtThisSco.text: This setting is set at the server only.

web.administration.settings.changeOnItsP.text: Change it on the sign-in mode page

web.administration.settings.onItsOwnPage.text: The sign-in mode is changed on its own page.

web.administration.setting.analysis.sign.text: The significance level (alpha) of the analysis of variance and the mean comparison: above 0 and below 1; 0.05 by convention.

web.administration.setting.analysis.mean.text: The test that separates the treatment means: protectedLSD (Fisher's LSD only after a significant F test), lsd, tukeyHSD, or dunnett (each treatment against the check).

web.administration.setting.analysis.miss.text: What an analysis does with a plot that has no value. refuse: the analysis stops and names the missing plots.

web.administration.setting.identity.sign.text: open: everyone who reaches the server may do everything. accounts: each person signs in and holds the roles given to them.

web.administration.setting.identity.sess.text: How many hours a sign-in lasts before the person signs in again: 1 to 720.

web.administration.setting.identity.work.text: The audience every trusted workload's token must name: this server's own name for itself, usually its address. While it is not set, no workload token is accepted.

web.administration.setting.tasks.timeZon.text: The time zone schedules are read in, an IANA name such as UTC or Africa/Nairobi.

web.administration.setting.tasks.maximum.text: How many task runs the scheduler lets go at once: 1 to 64.

web.administration.setting.tasks.runRete.text: How many days a task's run records are kept: 1 to 3650.

web.administration.signInMode.about.open.text: No sign-in. Everyone who reaches the server may do everything. For one person on their own machine.

web.administration.signInMode.about.acco.text: Every person signs in and holds the roles given to them. It needs an active account that is administrator at the server first.

web.administration.signInMode.confirmOpe.text: Yes, open the server to everyone who can reach it (needed only when choosing Open)

web.administration.confirm.group.warning.text: This deletes the group. Its members stay, but they lose every role the group gave them. It cannot be undone.

web.administration.confirm.workload.warn.text: This removes the rule and every role given to it. Jobs that relied on it are refused from then on. It cannot be undone.

web.administration.confirm.task.warning.text: This deletes the task and the record of all its runs. It cannot be undone.

web.administration.confirm.task.kept.text: This task is kept for the identity provider {provider} and is not deleted while that provider uses it.

web.refused.intro.text: Your account does not hold the permission this needs there, so nothing was done.

web.refused.whatNext.text: A person who manages access here can give you a role that holds it.

web.notFound.intro.text: This is not here, or it is not yours to see.

web.administration.providers.nameHelp.text: A lower-case letter, then 1 to 31 lower-case letters, digits or '-'. It becomes part of addresses and cannot be changed.

web.administration.providers.addIntro.text: Choose the kind of provider. A provider's secret is never typed here: its settings name the environment variable that holds it.

web.administration.provider.about.openID.text: Sign-in through an OpenID Connect provider, such as Entra ID, Keycloak or Google.

web.administration.provider.about.saml.text: Sign-in through one SAML 2.0 identity provider.

web.administration.provider.about.ldap.text: Sign-in with a directory's user name and password, such as Active Directory.

web.administration.provider.about.scim.text: The provider creates, updates and deactivates accounts and groups here; nobody signs in through it.

web.administration.provider.about.samlFe.text: Sign-in through the institutions of a research and education federation, such as eduGAIN.

web.administration.provider.about.cas.text: Sign-in through an Apereo CAS server.

web.administration.provider.isEnabled.text: Enabled: people sign in, or are provisioned, through it.

web.administration.provider.isDisabled.text: Disabled: nobody signs in, and nothing is provisioned, through it. Its settings and links are kept.

web.administration.provider.registerIntr.text: What the provider's own administrator is given. The addresses must lead to this server.

web.administration.provider.tokenIntro.text: The bearer token the provider sends with each provisioning request. Issuing a new one replaces the old one at once. Only its hash is kept, so it is shown once.

web.administration.provider.tokenShownOn.text: The new provisioning token, shown this once; copy it now:

web.administration.provider.settingsIntr.text: The settings as they were added.

web.administration.provider.help.newAcco.text: What a sign-in does when the provider's identity is linked to no account yet: refuse it (an administrator or provisioning makes the account first), create an account from what the provider says, or linkByUserName to the account with the same user name.

web.administration.provider.help.groups.text: ignore the provider's groups, or mirror them as groups named <provider>/<group> whose members only the provider sets.

web.administration.provider.help.certifi.text: A PEM file on the server with the certificate authority to trust for this address, when it is not one the system already trusts. Empty: the system's own.

web.administration.provider.help.signOut.text: Signing out here also signs the person out at the provider.

web.administration.provider.help.signedO.text: Where the provider sends the person after signing out everywhere (https). Needs signOutEverywhere.

web.administration.provider.help.issuer.text: The provider's issuer address (https), as its discovery document names it.

web.administration.provider.help.clientI.text: The client ID the provider gave this server.

web.administration.provider.help.clientS.text: The name of the environment variable that holds the client secret. The secret itself is never stored here.

web.administration.provider.help.returnU.text: This server's address the provider sends the person back to: https://<this server>/signin/with/<provider name>/return

web.administration.provider.help.signing.text: The key that signs this server's SAML requests and logout messages. Needed for single logout.

web.administration.provider.help.decrypt.text: The keys that decrypt assertions encrypted to this server. The first is the current one; keep an older one while the provider still encrypts to it.

web.administration.provider.help.keyFile.text: The PEM file of the private key, on the server.

web.administration.provider.help.certifi.text: The PEM file of the key's certificate, on the server.

web.administration.provider.help.passwor.text: The name of the environment variable that holds the key file's password, if it has one.

web.administration.provider.help.allowCB.text: Also accept assertions encrypted with AES-CBC, for a provider that cannot use AES-GCM.

web.administration.provider.help.singleL.text: This server's address for the provider's logout messages: https://<this server>/signin/with/<provider name>/signout

web.administration.provider.help.metadat.text: The address of the identity provider's SAML metadata (https).

web.administration.provider.help.identit.text: Which entity of the metadata is the identity provider, when the metadata holds more than one.

web.administration.provider.help.entityI.text: The name this server goes by at the provider (its SAML entity ID), usually its address.

web.administration.provider.help.userNam.text: The attribute that holds the person's user name.

web.administration.provider.help.display.text: The attribute that holds the person's display name.

web.administration.provider.help.emailAt.text: The attribute that holds the person's e-mail address.

web.administration.provider.help.groupsA.text: The attribute that lists the person's groups, for groups set to mirror.

web.administration.provider.help.mdqURL.text: The address of the federation's metadata query (MDQ) service (https).

web.administration.provider.help.signing.text: The PEM certificate whose key signs what is fetched from that address; everything fetched is checked against it.

web.administration.provider.help.institu.text: The entity IDs of the institutions offered here, one to a line. Leave empty when a discoveryAggregate is named.

web.administration.provider.help.discove.text: The federation's signed aggregate of all its members, to offer every one of them instead of a list of institutions. A scheduled task reads it every six hours.

web.administration.provider.help.subject.text: Which scoped identifier names a person: subjectID, pairwiseID or eduPersonPrincipalName.

web.administration.provider.help.organiz.text: The name of your organisation, published in this server's metadata.

web.administration.provider.help.informa.text: A page about this service, published in the metadata (https).

web.administration.provider.help.privacy.text: This service's privacy statement, published in the metadata (https).

web.administration.provider.help.technic.text: The technical contact published in the metadata, an e-mail address.

web.administration.provider.help.securit.text: The security contact published in the metadata, an e-mail address.

web.administration.provider.help.serverU.text: The address of the CAS server (https).

web.administration.provider.help.port.text: The port: 636 for LDAP over TLS, 389 with startTLS.

web.administration.provider.help.startTL.text: Connect in the clear and then switch to TLS (STARTTLS), instead of TLS from the start.

web.administration.provider.help.baseDN.text: The distinguished name below which people are searched for, such as dc=example,dc=org.

web.administration.provider.help.service.text: The account the server searches the directory as (a distinguished name or a user principal name).
The name of the environment variable that holds that account's password. The password itself is never stored here.

web.administration.provider.help.userAtt.text: The attribute a person's user name is matched against, such as sAMAccountName or uid.

web.administration.provider.help.baseURL.text: The https address the provider reaches this server's SCIM endpoint at, without a trailing slash: https://<this server>/scim/<provider name>/v2

web.administration.workloads.issuerHelp.text: One of these names: {named}; or the https address of an OpenID Connect issuer as its tokens name it, without a trailing slash.

web.administration.workloads.claimsHelp.text: One to a line, as claim=value. A token must carry each with exactly this value. A rule for GitHub Actions needs repository_id; one for GitLab.com needs project_id.

web.administration.workloads.audience.text: Every workload token must name the audience {audience}.

web.administration.workloads.noAudience.text: No rule can be added, and no workload token is accepted, until the server setting identity.workloadAudience is set.

web.administration.workload.fixed.text: What a rule trusts does not change. To trust something else, remove the rule and add a new one.

web.administration.workload.isEnabled.text: Enabled: a job whose token matches acts with this rule's roles.

web.administration.workload.isDisabled.text: Disabled: it accepts no token. Its roles wait until it is enabled again.

web.administration.tasks.kindsIntro.text: Choose the kind of task. A kind is code; a task is one configuration of it, with its own schedule.

web.administration.tasks.addIntro.text: The task starts enabled, with the kind's default schedule ({schedule}) and time limit ({minutes} minutes); change them on its page.

web.administration.tasks.nameHelp.text: A lower-case letter, then 1 to 63 letters, digits or '-'.

web.administration.audit.actorHelp.text: Who: a user name, a task or a workload rule exactly as the list shows it, or operator or everyone.

web.administration.audit.actionHelp.text: Action: a whole action or its beginning, such as role.assign, or task. for every task action.

web.administration.audit.dateHelp.text: Dates are days in UTC, written year-month-day, such as 2026-03-31. Times in the list are UTC.

web.administration.audit.notADate.text: {field}: “{typed}” is not a date written year-month-day.

web.signIn.search.hint.text: Type part of its name, its web domain or its entity ID.

web.signIn.search.notLoaded.text: The list of institutions has not been loaded yet. Try again later, or ask the site's administrator.

web.signIn.search.more.text: More institutions match than the first {count} shown; type more of the name to narrow them.

web.received.intro.text: Every file an import read is kept here exactly as it came, with the columns as they were mapped. The files stand beside the trial; they are not part of its content hash.

web.received.none.text: No file has been imported into this trial yet.

web.received.bundleIntro.text: A bundle is the trial's JSON document with these files and a manifest beside it, in one zip archive. Importing it into another store restores the files too.

web.received.bundle.text: Download the trial with its files

web.retention.trial.closingIntro.text: The closed date is what retention counts from where a rule keeps something until the trial is closed. Closing changes nothing else.

web.retention.trial.held.text: This trial is under a hold: nothing of it is pruned, and it cannot be deleted.

web.retention.trial.notHeld.text: This trial is under no hold.

web.retention.done.hold.text: The trial is under a hold.

web.retention.intro.text: What this store holds, how long each kind of data is kept, and what the rules now let go. Nothing leaves until a rule says so: every area is kept unless its rule is changed.

web.retention.areas.intro.text: Sizes are the bytes of the content held, not the space the database uses for it.

web.retention.area.trialRecords.holds.text: Each trial as its record: design, layout and values. A record leaves only whole.

web.retention.area.receivedFiles.holds.text: The files imports read, kept exactly as they came.

web.retention.area.auditLog.holds.text: Every change, who made it and from where.

web.retention.area.sessionsAndTokens.hol.text: Sessions, API tokens, sign-ins waiting for a provider, and messages used once. Only expired ones ever leave.

web.retention.area.taskRuns.holds.text: The record of each run of a scheduled task, with its output.

web.retention.settingHelp.text: A rule is a setting, changed by someone who may manage retention: keep, keepFor:<period> or keepUntilClosed:<period>, with a period such as P90D, P18M or P5Y. The rules of trial records, received files and the audit log can also be set for a place or a trial.

web.retention.rule.keepUntilClosed.text: Keep until the trial is closed, then for {period}

web.retention.withTheTrialRecord.text: These leave with the trial's record.

web.retention.holds.intro.text: A trial under a hold loses nothing to pruning and cannot be deleted. A hold is set and released on the trial's page.

web.retention.holds.none.text: No trial is under a hold.

web.retention.pruning.intro.text: Pruning removes what the rules let go and records what went in the audit log. It also runs every day as a scheduled task.

web.retention.preview.would.text: Pruning now would remove exactly this:

web.retention.preview.nothing.text: Nothing would be pruned now: no rule lets anything go.

web.retention.prune.confirmIntro.text: This removes everything listed below for good. It cannot be undone.

web.retention.outcome.done.text: This was removed, and recorded in the audit log:

web.retention.outcome.nothing.text: Nothing was pruned: no rule lets anything go.
